maya: heads-up — spike on shared-pool-rg3 at ~14:12Z, 95th jumped from 80ms -> 320ms for a short window. tenant acme-prod impacted. looks like a kernel/module swap + recompile during a burst reclaim. anyone seeing this elsewhere?

raj: saw same cluster graphs, but only on nodes with mixed small/large sequences. can you paste the trace?

maya: pasted short trace below, captured with runtime-trace v2.2:
```
[14:12:03] req=acme-prod seq=2048 kernel=matmul_v2 -> swapping to matmul_v2_fp8_opt
[14:12:03] start recompile(krnl=matmul_v2_fp8_opt) pid=7123
[14:12:03] kv-cache miss set=acme-prod prefix=0.4s
[14:12:04] completed recompile latency=180ms
[14:12:04] first-token latency jump -> p95 drain
```

sophie: interesting that kv-cache miss and recompile coincide. maybe batching heuristic pushed larger sequences to a kernel variant that wasn't JIT-warmed?

dylan: bench-bot triggered a reclaim around 14:11:58 to make room for a burst from tenant=glint-inc — that reclaim evicted some shared model slots. ops-bot logs: `reclaim:evict slots=6 pool=rg3 reason=burst-reserve`.

bench-bot: alert posted to #incidents at 14:12:05 — SLO p95 > 250ms for 3m.

raj: hypothesis: batching heuristic grouped a few long sequences into a path that selects the FP8-optimized kernel; because nobody had warmed that kernel on that GPU recently, runtime triggered a lazy compile during the critical path. eviction earlier removed the warm kernels from the slot, so recompile cost hit acme-prod.

maya: reproduce steps I'm trying locally: 1) force eviction of model slots with `poolctl evict --slots 6`, 2) send a burst of long seq requests with `rt-bench --seq 2048 --concurrency 4`, 3) observe recompile cost.

sophie: can we mitigate ASAP? options: A) pre-warm FP8 kernel variants on shared pools during low-load, B) adjust batching heuristic to avoid switching kernel variant mid-burst, C) soft-block evictions if a kernel has active compile ops.

dylan: provisional fix: added a small cooldown — do not evict slots that reported recent compile activity (<5m). rolled to rg3 as a canary at 14:30Z. monitoring now.

maya: after cooldown rollout, p95 back to baseline within 6m. still want a follow-up: profile how often kernel selection flips for mixed-seq workloads and add a telemetry tag `compile_reason` to traces.

raj: agree. action items: (1) add `compile_reason` + kernel_warm_metric (owner: eng-runtime, sophie) (2) iterate batching heuristic to prefer warm kernels for spike-sensitive tenants (owner: maya) (3) evaluate soft-evict cooldown default (owner: dylan). I'll file tickets.

ops-bot: ticket created: INF-4882 "warm-kernel telemetry + batching warm-pref" assigned to eng-runtime.

maya: thanks everyone :thumbsup: I'll follow up with a short postmortem and add the reproduce script to the runbook.
